Of E's neighbors, C and F match E's value of 3 and are filled in accent; D and G differ, and B matches but is not a neighbor, so it is faded." width="100%"} Looks at the direct neighbors of a starting node and returns those whose numeric attribute value falls inside a window around the starting node's own value. The window can be set as an absolute offset (`tol_abs=`), as a percentage of the starting value (`tol_pct=`), or left unset for exact matching. Both tolerances take a `(below, above)` pair, so the window can be asymmetric. This is useful for: - finding homophilous ties, e.g., friends of similar age or trading partners of similar size - checking whether a node's value is in line with its local neighborhood (a node with no similar neighbors may be an outlier) - seeding local, attribute-aware expansions such as region growing on spatial graphs Neighbors are taken with `mode="all"`, so in a directed graph both predecessors and successors are considered. Only one hop is examined and the selection is not changed. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The starting node, given as an integer node ID or a string label. Its value of `node_attr=` sets the center of the similarity window. An unknown ID or label raises `ValueError`. [node_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the node attribute to compare. The starting node's value must be numeric (an `int` or `float`), otherwise `ValueError` is raised. If the starting node does not have this attribute at all, the result is an empty list. Neighbors that lack the attribute, or whose value is not numeric, are silently skipped. [tol_abs]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, float] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Absolute tolerance as a `(lower, upper)` tuple of non-negative offsets. With a starting value `x`, neighbors whose value lies in `[x - lower, x + upper]` (inclusive) are returned. For example, `(1.0, 2.0)` accepts values from `x - 1.0` to `x + 2.0`. Defaults to `None`. Give at most one of `tol_abs=` and `tol_pct=`. [tol_pct]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, float] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Percentage tolerance as a `(lower_pct, upper_pct)` tuple, expressed in percent (so `10` means 10%) of the magnitude of `x`. Neighbors whose value lies in `[x - |x| * lower_pct / 100, x + |x| * upper_pct / 100]` are returned. For example, `(10, 20)` accepts values from `0.9 * x` to `1.2 * x` when `x` is positive, and from `-110` to `-80` when `x` is `-100`. Defaults to `None`. Because the window scales with `x`, it is suited to attributes that span several orders of magnitude, but it collapses to exact matching when `x` is `0`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node IDs of the neighbors whose attribute value falls within the window, in the order returned by `get_neighbors()`. Empty if the starting node lacks the attribute, has no neighbors, or no neighbor is in range. When neither `tol_abs=` nor `tol_pct=` is set, only neighbors with exactly the same value are returned. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the starting node's value for `node_attr=` exists but is not numeric (`int` or `float`), if `node=` is an ID or label not found in the graph, if both `tol_abs=` and `tol_pct=` are given, or if a tolerance offset is negative. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Let $x_u$ be the starting node's value. With `tol_abs=(a, b)`, a neighbor $v$ is similar when $x_u - a \le x_v \le x_u + b$. With `tol_pct=(p, q)` it is similar when $x_u - |x_u| p/100 \le x_v \le x_u + |x_u| q/100$. With neither, the condition reduces to $x_v = x_u$. Bounds are inclusive on both sides. Python `bool` values are a subclass of `int` and are therefore treated as numeric (`True == 1`). ## Examples {.doc-examples} Only "B" falls within ±1.0 of "A"'s value of `5.0`; "C" at `10.0` is far outside that range: ::: {#efa31028 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_nodes([("A", {"value": 5.0}), ("B", {"value": 5.5}), ("C", {"value": 10.0})]) graph.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C")]) similar = graph.get_similar_neighbors("A", "value", tol_abs=(1.0, 1.0)) [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in similar] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['B'] ``` ::: ::: Percentage tolerance scales with the starting value instead of using a fixed range -- here ±20% of `5.0` covers `4.0` to `6.0`, which includes "B" at `4.5` but still excludes "C": ::: {#4a9c64e1 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes([("A", {"value": 5.0}), ("B", {"value": 4.5}), ("C", {"value": 10.0})]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C")]) ) similar_pct = graph.get_similar_neighbors("A", "value", tol_pct=(20, 20)) [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in similar_pct] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['B'] ``` ::: ::: An asymmetric window looks in one direction only. In this small trade network, `tol_abs=(0, 50)` asks for partners of "Acme" that are the same size or up to 50 larger -- "Big" (`140`) qualifies, while "Small" (`60`) is below the window, and without any tolerance only the exact match "Twin" comes back: ::: {#d61293f2 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} trade = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="Acme", revenue=100) .add_node(label="Small", revenue=60) .add_node(label="Big", revenue=140) .add_node(label="Twin", revenue=100) .add_edges([("Acme", "Small"), ("Acme", "Big"), ("Acme", "Twin")]) ) up = trade.get_similar_neighbors("Acme", "revenue", tol_abs=(0, 50)) exact = trade.get_similar_neighbors("Acme", "revenue") ( sorted(trade.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in up), [trade.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in exact], ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (['Big', 'Twin'], ['Twin']) ``` ::: :::
